title: Storyboard relay
note: Muse establishes the postal robot. Nano Banana stages the next scene but duplicates its seedling. Gemini identifies that error; Muse Edit receives both frames and the critique, removes the duplicate plant and improves the pose. A fresh Gemini review still flags the closed hatch. This is a fixed revision demonstration with visible limits, not a guarantee of perfect continuity.

inputs.label: First scene
inputs.text: First frame of an original two-scene story. A tiny postal robot has a rounded cream enamel body, one round amber eye, short dark-blue legs, and an orange mail satchel. It carries one clear glass capsule containing a single bright-green seedling. Outside a locked circular hatch of an abandoned orbital greenhouse, the robot reaches toward the small mechanical latch beside the door with one gripper while holding the capsule securely with the other. Dormant vines are visible through frosted glass; a curved station window reveals a black starfield. Wide 3:2 medium shot with the full robot, capsule and hatch visible. Tactile stop-motion miniature photography, indigo shadows and warm amber practical light. One robot and one capsule. No lettering, captions, split screen, panel borders or watermark.

inputs.label: Next beat
inputs.text: Create the next story beat inside the greenhouse. The robot is now crouched beside a circular soil tray, carefully placing the same bright-green seedling into the soil with one gripper; its other gripper holds the opened, now-empty glass capsule. The orange satchel remains visible. The round hatch stands open behind it. Frame the planting action clearly in a new medium shot. This is a visibly different action and location within the same world, not a restyle or wider crop of the doorway scene. Retain the tactile miniature look and indigo/amber light. No lettering or extra characters.

inputs.label: Continuity rules
inputs.text: Keep the same robot's rounded cream body, single round amber eye, dark-blue legs, orange satchel and relative proportions. Track the one glass capsule and one green seedling: the closed capsule in frame 1 should be opened and empty during planting in frame 2, with no duplicate seedling or capsule. Keep the miniature materials and indigo/amber lighting recognizable. Frame 1 shows an arrival at a closed hatch; frame 2 must clearly show planting inside after the hatch opens.

outputs.label: 2. Nano Banana: the draft duplicates the seedling

alternates.title: A crab catches the wind

inputs.label: First scene
inputs.text: First frame of an original two-scene story. A small red crab kite-maker stands on a sun-bleached wooden jetty over a shallow turquoise salt lagoon. It has two large claws, four small walking legs visible, round black eyes, and a floppy straw hat with a violet ribbon. One claw holds a wound white string reel; beside it rests a single yellow diamond kite with exactly two violet tail bows. The crab looks toward a flat pink sandbar across the water. Bold cut-paper collage, crisp torn-paper edges, coral-red, yellow, turquoise and pale pink, bright overhead sun. Wide 3:2 composition; entire crab, reel, kite and jetty visible. No robots, space stations, glass capsules, plants, text, panel borders or watermark.

inputs.label: Next beat
inputs.text: Create the next story beat on the pink sandbar across the lagoon. The same crab braces its legs and leans backward as the yellow diamond kite lifts overhead in a strong breeze. The white string visibly connects the kite to the reel in one claw; the other claw keeps the straw hat from blowing away. Exactly two violet bows remain on the kite's tail. Show the kite fully in frame and make the new wind-driven action clear. Retain the crisp cut-paper collage and sunlit coral/yellow/turquoise/pink palette. This is a new story action, not the original jetty picture with a changed background. No extra crabs or kites, lettering or panel borders.

inputs.label: Continuity rules
inputs.text: Preserve the red crab's body shape, black eyes, two claws, straw hat and violet ribbon. Keep one yellow diamond kite, two violet tail bows, and the white reel/string. The string should connect reel and kite in frame 2; the kite must be flying rather than resting. The scene moves from a wooden jetty to a pink sandbar. Preserve cut-paper materials, crisp edges and bright sunlit palette; do not inherit any robot, greenhouse or space-scene details.

title: Idea to concept art to 3D model
note: GLM 5.3 Flash turns a one-line object idea into a concept description: a teal capsule-shaped toy submarine with a cream belly band, a brass periscope, three cream-rimmed portholes, a brass wind-up key, and a striped tail cone with a three-blade propeller. Join adds fixed render rules (one whole object, three-quarter view, plain light-gray background, no props), and Muse paints the concept. TRELLIS.2 (1024 geometry, 1024 textures, about 80k faces) turns that single picture into a 3.6 MB textured GLB. Orbiting it in nanoodle's 3D viewer shows a complete toy from every side, including a far side and back that the picture never showed: portholes on both flanks, the striped tail, the propeller blades, the key, and the periscope. Flaws: the viewer renders it flatter and less glossy than the concept, the thin key and propeller blades go soft at some angles, and the cream band on the far side is a plainer flat strip. Inspired by @patchmonkeydev's prompt → concept → multi-view → 3D ComfyUI pipeline on X; no media from that post is used.

title: Blockout first, then the shot
note: GLM 5.3 Flash writes three prompts from one action idea: a grayscale blockout prompt, a look bible, and a motion brief. Join puts a fixed keep-composition line in front of the look bible and a short animate line in front of the motion brief. Muse paints the blockout: matte gray rooftops and one boxy wheel-legged robot mid-leap over the gap, seen from a low rooftop camera. Muse Edit restyles it into weathered brick, fire escapes, a dusk sky, and an off-white robot with orange panels, keeping the blockout's layout, robot pose, and camera; it also adds a flock of pigeons that the look bible asked for. Seedance 1.5 Pro (720p, 5 s, silent) animates the finished still: the robot sails over the gap, spins sideways in mid-air, lands on the far roof, and the camera swings round behind it as it rolls toward the sunset. Flaws: the mid-air spin was not asked for, the landing has no crouch-and-settle, and the robot keeps rolling instead of holding still. Inspired by ComfyUI's blockout-then-restyle post on X; no media from that post is used.

title: Mix the references
review: All four references land in one coherent shot
note: Four Muse stills stand in for your own uploads: a paper-craft fox (image 1), a yellow knitted raincoat (image 2), a red paper lantern (image 3) and a paper harbor pier at dusk (image 4). FLUX.3 Klein Edit gets them in port order (image, image2, image3, image4), and the mix instruction names each one by number. In the result the fox wears the same raincoat with its three wooden toggles and holds the one lantern by its bamboo handle while standing on the cardboard pier, with the striped lighthouse behind it. Flaws: the two paper boats from image 4 mostly drop out, the fox's ears poke through the hood, and the coat comes out longer than the flat-lay reference. A first prompt without “exactly one lantern” gave the fox two lanterns, so the instruction now says it outright. Swap any reference Image node for a 📷 Image input to mix your own photos. Checked outputs are SFW (no people). Inspired by the multi-reference workflows ComfyUI showed for Krea 3 and FLUX.3 Klein (https://x.com/ComfyUI/status/2110840667337642330); no media from that post is used.

inputs.text:
Make one new picture that combines the four reference images.
Image 1 is the character: keep this exact paper-craft fox, same folded orange paper, white chest, black nose and eyes, same proportions.
Image 2 is the outfit: dress the fox in this exact yellow knitted raincoat, with the same pointed hood up and the same three wooden toggles.

Everything stays paper-craft. The lantern casts warm light on the raincoat. One fox only, no other characters, no text.
